title: Connect the WhatsApp channel
description: Connect your business number through Meta's window and start receiving customer conversations.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Settings & channels”, then open the “Channels” tab.

steps.title: Open Channels
steps.body: From Settings & channels open the Channels tab, then choose WhatsApp.

steps.title: Start the Meta connection
steps.body: Press the connect button and sign in with the Meta account that has permission to manage your business.

steps.title: Choose the business and number
steps.body: Follow Meta's window to choose the business portfolio, the WhatsApp account and the phone number, and complete the required verification.

steps.title: Check the connection
steps.body: Go back to Channels and check the connection status. Send a message from another number and confirm it appears in Conversations.

title: Connect Salla and set up WhatsApp notifications
description: Learn the store connection requirements and where to set up order and abandoned-cart notifications. Completing the connection needs the app set up and the store's authorization.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Settings & channels”, then open the “Integrations” tab.

steps.title: Open Integrations
steps.body: Open Integrations, then the Salla settings. Connecting the store and connecting the WhatsApp channel are two separate steps; a WhatsApp connection alone does not connect the store.

steps.title: Connect the store
steps.body: From the connection tab we review the store status. “Not connected” means the store has not been linked to this account. If it says the app details are not configured, connecting is unavailable on this server until they are prepared; this does not mean WhatsApp is disconnected.

steps.title: Set up notifications
steps.body: Here we prepare order notifications and choose the templates. In the recorded account the store is not connected, so we only explain the setup; sending requires the store, WhatsApp and an approved template to be connected.

steps.title: Set up carts and test
steps.body: We open abandoned carts and review the delay, the number of reminders and the template. These are pre-launch settings; once the store is actually authorized we test with a sample cart and check that the message arrives.

description: Send conversation results to your connected ad platform.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Settings & channels”, then open the “Integrations” tab.

steps.title: Choose the ad platform
steps.body: Open Integrations, then the card of the ad platform you use.

steps.title: Complete the connection
steps.body: Connect the account with the required permissions. The connection options may differ by platform and by how widely its app is available.

steps.title: Open event mapping
steps.body: Choose the “Event mapping” tab and review the settings and the fields the platform requires before turning sending on.

steps.title: Test the result

title: Auto-reply: buttons and builder tools explained
description: Get hands-on with choosing the channel, the library, the diagram and the edit, save and run tools.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Auto-reply”.

steps.title: Choosing the channel
steps.body: The WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram and other buttons change the channel whose flow you are editing; each channel has its own flow and its own on/off switch.

steps.title: Library filter: All and Steps
steps.body: “All” shows every card, and “Steps” shows the single steps such as the welcome and the services menu.

steps.title: Full flows filter
steps.body: “Full flows” shows templates made of several linked steps. The + button on a card adds it straight to the diagram.

steps.title: Add a ready-made flow
steps.body: We press + on “Full customer service flow”. The welcome, menu, prices, order follow-up and transfer steps appear already linked.

steps.title: Zoom out, zoom in and re-center
steps.body: The − button zooms the diagram out, the + button zooms it in, and the ⌖ button restores the default zoom and position. These buttons don't change the steps' content.

steps.title: Edit a step
steps.body: Press a step card on the diagram to open its form. The step name only shows on the diagram, while the message text is what the customer sees.

steps.title: Change the type and the link
steps.body: The “Step type” list sets the action. “Link to step” sets what follows; you can also link by dragging from the dot on the step's side to the step you want.

steps.title: Add and remove an option
steps.body: In a list step write the question and the options. “Add option” creates a row, and × deletes the option. Each option has its own list to link the next step.

steps.title: Move-step arrows
steps.body: The left, right, up and down buttons move the step's position. You can also move the card by dragging it on the diagram.

steps.title: Save the change and close
steps.body: “Save changes” saves the step's content. “Close” or × closes the window. Check the save-success message before you carry on.

steps.title: Delete the step
steps.body: “Delete step” removes the step from the flow; review the flow and its links afterwards. We show it here on an extra training step only.

steps.title: Turning on and off
steps.body: The “Auto-reply off/on” switch turns the selected channel's flow on or off. Test from another account before turning it on for customers.

title: Create and run an automation
description: Choose the trigger, conditions and actions, then test the rule before turning it on.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Automations”.

steps.title: Open Automations
steps.body: Go to Automations and start a new rule with a name that explains its purpose.

steps.title: Choose the trigger and conditions
steps.body: Set when the rule runs, then add suitable conditions such as the channel, the tag or the conversation status.

steps.title: Set the actions
steps.body: Add the action you need, such as sending a message or assigning a team. Review the order of the actions and the message contents.

steps.title: Test, then turn it on
steps.body: Use “Test a message” to check the rule. When it's ready choose “Run the rule after saving”, then “Save and run”.

steps.body: Open Conversations and pick the channel or search for the customer you need.

steps.title: Review and reply
steps.body: Read the message history and the customer's details, then write your reply and send it through the available channel.

steps.title: Organize the follow-up
steps.body: Use assignment, status and tags according to your permissions, and check that the changes were saved.

steps.title: Follow the approval

title: Build a full auto-reply from scratch
description: We build a welcome message and an options list, and connect each option to the right reply or team.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Auto-reply”.

steps.title: Start with a custom step
steps.body: Choose WhatsApp, then press “Custom step”. We will build the flow manually instead of using a ready template.

steps.title: Write the welcome
steps.body: Choose “Send a message”. Name the step “Store welcome” and write: Welcome, how can we help you? Then press “Add step”.

steps.title: Add the prices reply
steps.body: Add a new message step named “Prices”, write the service details, then save it.

steps.title: Add the transfer to support
steps.body: Add a step of type “Transfer to a team” and choose the customer service team. Prepare the team first from the Teams page if it doesn't appear.

steps.title: Create the options list
steps.body: Add “Send a short list”, write the customer's question, then a “Prices” option and a “Talk to support” option.

steps.title: Link each option
steps.body: From the first option's link list choose “Prices”, and from the second option's link choose the support transfer step, then add the step.

steps.title: Link the welcome to the list
steps.body: Open the welcome step, choose the list in “Link to step”, then save the change.

steps.title: Review and turn on
steps.body: Review the arrows, the options and the customer-facing texts, then turn on the auto-reply switch for the channel. The account in the video is a training account and doesn't send to real customers.

title: Every auto-reply step type
description: A hands-on look at all thirteen types and the fields specific to each.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Auto-reply”.

steps.title: Send a message
steps.body: Write the step name and the message text, and set what follows from “Link to step”.

steps.title: Send an image
steps.body: Upload an image from the file field, add an optional caption, then choose what follows.

steps.title: Send a video
steps.body: Upload a video that suits the channel and the limit shown, add a description, then what follows.

steps.title: Send a document
steps.body: Upload the document you need and add a caption if you want, then link it to a next step.

steps.title: Send a short list
steps.body: Write the question and add the options; each option has a text and a next step. Use the number the channel accepts.

steps.title: Send a long list
steps.body: Use it for more options and link each option to its path. Review the channel's limits before publishing.

steps.title: Knowledge Base reply
steps.body: Prepare the questions and answers in the knowledge base. Write the no-match reply and link a follow-up step when needed.

steps.title: Automatic AI reply
steps.body: Requires your account's AI provider key and a knowledge base. It sends the reply automatically; link a hand-over to an employee for when there is no answer.

steps.title: Show the catalog
steps.body: Add the products from the Catalog and set the intro message. The next step is used when an employee is requested or there are no products.

steps.title: Nearest branch
steps.body: Prepare the branch data and write the location request message. The bot sends the nearest branch according to the customer's location.

steps.title: Transfer to a team
steps.body: Choose an existing team. This is a final step that moves the conversation to the team with no automatic follow-up afterwards.

steps.title: Transfer to an employee
steps.body: Choose the specific employee. Prepare the employee and their permissions first; this is a final step.

steps.title: Close the conversation
steps.body: You can write an optional closing message and then close the conversation. Don't link it to a next step.

title: API: creating and managing the key

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Settings & channels”, then open the “Developers” tab.

steps.title: Open Developers
steps.body: From Settings & channels choose “Developers”. This page needs a permission and a plan that supports the feature.

steps.title: Create a key with a clear name
steps.body: Write a name that explains the integration, then press “Create key”. The video uses a training key that is revoked after recording.

steps.title: Copy and hide the key
steps.body: The key shows only once. “Copy” copies it and “Hide” hides it from the screen. Don't put your key in the website interface or in public recordings.

steps.title: Revoke the key
steps.body: The “Revoke” button stops this key being accepted after you confirm. Update the connected system with a replacement key when needed.

title: API: a real request and reading the result
description: We test reading customers with a training key and see the server's actual response.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Settings & channels”, then open the “Developers” tab.

steps.title: Open the documentation
steps.body: From the Developers tab open the full API documentation or the OpenAPI specification. The production base URL is https://linklysa.io/api/v1.

steps.title: Prepare the request
steps.body: We use GET /api/v1/customers?limit=5 with Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY. We keep the key on the server and never show it to users.

steps.title: Run the request and read the result
steps.body: We run the request against the local server with a training account. The HTTP code and the real response appear; ok: true means the request succeeded, and data holds the customers and the paging data.

title: API: authentication and validation errors
description: See real responses for a request without a key and a customer request with missing data.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Settings & channels”, then open the “Developers” tab.

steps.title: A request without a key
steps.body: We run a GET for customers without Authorization; the server returns HTTP 401 because the key is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: A request with missing data
steps.body: We run a POST for customers with a training key and an empty body; the server returns HTTP 400 and explains that phone and name are required.

steps.title: Review the limits and fix the request
steps.body: Use Bearer with a single space and then the correct key, and send the required fields. On 429 wait for the Retry-After duration; we don't use up the request limit in this recording.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Settings & channels”, then open the “Developers” tab.

steps.title: Set the receiving URL
steps.body: From Developers open the Webhooks section. Enter a public HTTPS URL that belongs to your system, not a dashboard page link.

steps.title: Choose the events
steps.body: Choose “Message received”, “Conversation closed” or “New lead” according to what the integration needs, then press “Add webhook” in your real account after preparing the receiver.

steps.title: Managing the webhook
steps.body: In the registered row you will see the pause/enable, delivery log and delete buttons. The recording shows a local training example and doesn't connect to an external receiver.

steps.title: The signature and the delivery log
steps.body: Your system receives the signing secret on creation; store it safely and verify the HMAC signature as the documentation describes. Review the HTTP code, the result and the time in the delivery log.

title: API: add a customer and verify it in the interface
description: Send a real POST with training data and see the customer on the Customers page.

steps.title: Choose the page from the sidebar
steps.body: From the sidebar choose “Settings & channels”, then open the “Developers” tab.

steps.title: Prepare the customer data
steps.body: We use POST /api/v1/customers with name and phone in a valid Saudi number format. The number shown is a training number and no messages are sent to it.

steps.title: Run the request
steps.body: We send JSON with a training key, and show the server's real response with the customer ID, name and mobile.

steps.title: Check in Customers
steps.body: We choose Customers & tags from the sidebar, refresh the page to fetch the latest data, then search for the name “API test customer” to check that the record was really added to the training account.

code:
curl -X POST "https://linklysa.io/api/v1/customers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Customer name","phone":"9665XXXXXXXX"}'
